summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive web field guide for school-age and casual space fans. A Moon and Mars map shows six machines left behind since 1967: Surveyor 3, Lunokhod 1, the Apollo 17 Moon Buggy, Viking 1, Spirit and Opportunity. Tap one and it tells its own story in the first person, then explains how it was built, what science it made possible, and when it last called home. It answers the challenge by turning dense mission history into an engaging story, with real facts and a source on every card.
details: What it does Visitors pick a machine from a Moon or Mars map, or from a strip at the top of the page. Each machine tells its story in its own voice, followed by how it was built, what it made possible, and key numbers with its last signal. Every card links to its source. How it works The project is one self-contained web page built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The map is a schematic drawn in code, with pins placed by position. Selecting a machine updates the story card and the page address, so a single machine can be linked directly. The page works on phones and laptops, in light and dark themes, with large type and keyboard-friendly buttons. Benefits Learners meet real hardware and real science through a story instead of a list of facts. Teachers get six short, sourced missions across the Moon and Mars. The stories connect engineering to discovery. For example, a laser reflector on Lunokhod 1 returned light to Earth in 2010, about 40 years after the rover went quiet. What we hope to achieve We want students to feel a personal connection to these robotic explorers and to see that finished missions still teach us. Next we would add more machines, audio narration and a short classroom quiz. Tools used HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Google Fonts (Bricolage Grotesque, Atkinson Hyperlegible, JetBrains Mono). Claude, an AI assistant from Anthropic, for research help, story text and code. NASA mission pages and news reports for fact checking. A 7-slide deck for the demo.
